request:
I run a small tailoring shop in Kumasi and I want to keep my orders in order. I need to save each customer with their name, phone number and their measurements: chest, waist, hip and length, all in inches. For a customer I take orders, and each order has the garment, the date it is due, the price and the deposit the customer has paid, in cedis. The deposit can never be more than the price. I want to see all the orders for one customer and look at a single order. I also want to see every order that is due on or before a date I choose, so I know what to finish first. When a customer picks up their clothes I mark the order as collected, and collected orders should no longer show in that due list.

The client's answers to your questions:
Q: Can an order be marked as collected if the customer still owes part of the price, or must it be fully paid first?
A: No preference: you decide.
Q: When a customer pays more money later, should you be able to update the deposit on an existing order, or does it stay fixed once the order is saved?
A: No preference: you decide.
Q: Should each phone number belong to only one customer, or can two customers share the same number?
A: No preference: you decide.

Where the client has no preference or did not answer, choose the simplest option and add nothing they did not ask for (no logins, PINs or extra required fields).
summary:
Your shop's backend is built and all 38 of my automated checks pass. It saves your data in a file called `tailoring.db` in the project folder.

**What you can do:**
- **`POST /customers`**: save a new customer with their name, phone number and chest, waist, hip and length in inches. Each customer gets a number automatically.
- **`GET /customers/{customerNumber}`**: see one customer's details and measurements.
- **`POST /customers/{customerNumber}/orders`**: save a new order for that customer with the garment, due date (written like 2025-03-10), price and deposit in cedis. Every order starts as not collected.
- **`GET /customers/{customerNumber}/orders`**: see all orders for one customer.
- **`GET /orders/{orderNumber}`**: see one order with all its details.
- **`GET /orders/due?onOrBefore=2025-03-15`**: see every order not yet collected that is due on or before the date you choose, earliest first.
- **`PATCH /orders/{orderNumber}/collected`**: mark an order as collected so it disappears from the due list.

**What it refuses:**
- A deposit bigger than the price.
- A price or deposit below zero.
- A customer with any detail missing or blank, or a measurement of zero or less.
- An order with any detail missing, or a due date that isn't a real date (for example 30 February).
- A due-list request without a real date.
- Orders for a customer who doesn't exist, and looking up or changing a customer or order that doesn't exist.

**The three choices I made for you, as agreed:**
- An order can be marked collected even if the customer still owes money.
- The deposit can't be changed once the order is saved.
- Two customers can share a phone number.

Tell me if you'd like any of these changed. My questions from the plan are still open too: would you like a list of all your customers or a way to search by name or phone, and should anyone else be kept from seeing customers' details?

plan.summary: A simple system for your tailoring shop in Kumasi. It keeps your customers, with their name, phone number and their chest, waist, hip and length measurements in inches. It also keeps each customer's orders, with the garment, due date, price and deposit in cedis. You can see all orders for one customer, look at a single order, and list every order due on or before a date you choose so you know what to finish first. When a customer picks up their clothes you mark the order as collected, and it then disappears from that due list. You had no preference on three questions, so I chose the simplest option each time. First, an order can be marked as collected even if part of the price is still owed. Second, the deposit is fixed once the order is saved, so there is no way to change it later. Third, two customers may share the same phone number. Tell me if you would like any of these changed. I have also added a way to look up a single customer so you can read their saved measurements. Questions for you: would you like a list of all your customers, or a way to find a customer by name or phone number? Should anyone besides you be kept from seeing customers' phone numbers and measurements?
